body: حسم جوزيه مورينيو، مدرب ريال مدريد، مصير لاعبه الشاب تياجو بيتاريش، خاصة بعد اهتمام فولهام بالحصول عليه. وبحسب " صحيفة آس "، فإن بيتاريش لن يغادر ريال مدريد، وسيكون لاعبًا إضافيًا تحت قيادة مورينيو. وطلب مورينيو، عدم رحيل بيتاريش، وسيعول عليه بمجرد تعافيه من إصابته، ولا ينوي عودته إلى فريق الكاستيا. وبغض النظر عن امتلاكه بطاقة تسجيل مع الكاستيا، فإن بيتاريش سيُعامل كلاعب في الفريق الأول.  وفضل مورينيو، بقاء بيتاريش، رغم وصول عروض مغرية للاعب بالفعل، وكان أبرزها فولهام، الذي يدربه ألفارو أربيلوا. وعاد بيتاريش، بعد تتويجه بطلًا مع منتخب إسبانيا تحت 19 عامًا، وهو يحمل فكرة واحدة فقط، تدور حول القتال وانتزاع مكانه في الميرنجي. وهكذا بدأ فترة الإعداد للموسم الجديد، لكن الانتكاسة المتمثلة في الإصابة، اعترضت طريقه، غير أن هذه الضربة لم تعطل مستقبله.  وسيكون على بيتاريش، خوض المعركة في خط الوسط، حيث يرى مورينيو أن لديه مكانًا مناسبًا. والمنافسة ستكون كبيرة للغاية، ففي طريقة 4-2-3-1 التي يعتمدها المدرب البرتغالي باستمرار، هناك مكان لتشواميني وفالفيردي وكامافينجا وبرناردو سيلفا في ثنائي الارتكاز، وسيكون هناك مكان أيضًا لتياجو بيتاريش.

title: GTA 6's Netflix deal forces us to ask: can you pirate an advertisement?
summary: Just when you thought videogame marketing couldn't get sillier, people are going to wind up stealing a trailer.
body: Let's be real, come August 27, the Grand Theft Auto 6 "extended look" is not going to be exclusive to Netflix for six hours as advertised. It's going to be exclusive to Netflix for however long it takes for someone to record it and distribute a torrent. You wouldn't download a car, but would you download an ad for a game about stealing cars? It would be, I've now had to consider, technically piracy to do so. title: Diablo 4's newest class barely made a splash with Lord of Hatred, but it's shaping up to be king of the next season

body: Nobody is particularly surprised anymore when the newest hero or class added to a game ends up being its strongest by far. You can't really be the new flavor of the month without some extra sauce. But sometimes developers don't get the balance right and the new toy gets left on the shelf for other, more exciting options. This is basically what happened when warlocks debuted in Diablo 4 alongside the release of its Lord of Hatred expansion earlier this year. Despite being a marquee feature of the expansion, warlocks were criminally underpowered compared to the rest of the roster. Other classes–with their newly juiced up skill trees—could smash their way through the game while warlocks were left to limp along in their wake. Normally, I wouldn't care that much if one class couldn't compete with another in a largely singleplayer game, but warlocks also suffered from having a number of skills that forced them to stand still to cast, disrupting the flow of combat. They were not only weaker than everyone else but clunkier, too—the last thing you want in a fast-paced action RPG like Diablo. body: Doom, one of the most influential videogames of all time, was famously distributed via the shareware model: The game's first chapter was completely free, and if you liked it, you sent id Software some money and they mailed you the remaining two episodes. What would sometimes happen in those pre-online days, though, is that less-than-scrupulous resellers would offer the shareware version for sale, even though it was meant to be free. For $5 (or whatever, it's been a while), you could take home the hot new shooter from the guys who made Wolfenstein —and sure, you weren't getting the whole thing, but whatever. It's still Doom. Do you want to play it or not? Though you may not use it, Valve thinks you should, "because it's, like, cool," and even recommends a couple of sweet shortcuts to use with it. Valve notes that you could turn gyro controls off and on, depending on how your fingers sit on the controller, and it points out that the activation threshold is adjustable. That means you could activate a shortcut with only a slight lift of the fingers, or by taking the whole hand off the controller. Activating and deactivating gyro controls to recenter your hand is apparently called "ratcheting". Valve likens it to picking up your mouse when it hits the end of your mousepad.
